descriptionChirho: To attach or associate oneself with a person or group, forming a social, communal, or relational bond. The most common NT use, describing people joining themselves to others in fellowship, discipleship, or social attachment. Used of the prodigal son attaching himself to a citizen (Luke 15:15), believers not daring to join the apostles (Acts 5:13), Philip joining the Ethiopian's chariot (Acts 8:29), Saul attempting to join the disciples (Acts 9:26), Peter warned against associating with Gentiles (Acts 10:28), converts joining Paul and Silas (Acts 17:34), one who joins a prostitute (1 Cor 6:16), and one who joins the Lord (1 Cor 6:17). Rendered Arabic التصق, Hebrew נִדְבַּק/הִצְטָרֵף, Korean 의지하다/붙다, Spanish unirse/juntarse.

To hold fast or adhere to something abstract such as moral good or virtue, expressing devoted commitment and faithful attachment. Used in Rom 12:9 where believers are exhorted to cling to what is good (κολλώμενοι τῷ ἀγαθῷ). Rendered Arabic مُلتصقين, Hebrew דְבֵקִים, Hindi चिपकते हुए, Korean 붙어 있으라, Spanish adhiriendoos.

To adhere or cling in a literal, physical sense, as dust or dirt sticking to the surface of one's body or feet. Used in Luke 10:11 where the disciples are instructed to wipe off even the dust that clings to their feet (τὸν κολληθέντα κονιορτόν) as a testimony against that city. Rendered Arabic اللاصق, Hebrew נִדְבָּק, Hindi लगी हुई, Korean 묻은, Spanish pegado.

To be united to one's spouse in the bond of marriage, echoing the Genesis creation ordinance that a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife. Used in Matt 19:5 (quoting Gen 2:24) where κολληθήσεται describes the marital union established by God. Rendered Arabic يلتصق, Hebrew יִדְבַּק, Hindi जुड़ेगा, Korean 연합하리라, Spanish se unirá.

To heap together or reach by accumulation, used metaphorically in Rev 18:5 of Babylon's sins being piled up or joined together reaching to heaven (ἐκολλήθησαν αὐτῆς αἱ ἁμαρτίαι). This represents a figurative extension of the physical 'sticking together' sense applied to the accumulation of transgressions. Rendered Arabic التصقت, Hebrew דָבְקוּ, Korean 쌍였다, Spanish se han amontonado.
